lessons.claim: When MET.observable(predicted=0.0), the percentage error (err_pct) becomes None to avoid a division by zero, and MET.judge() treated err_pct=None not as 'no verdict possible' but unconditionally as an implementation_check FAIL -- so an observable whose prediction is exactly 0 (for example a linear bending stiffness derived to be 0 by symmetry) is always misjudged as a bug regardless of the measured value. First found on chain-bend-2d-dlvo's K_prime (measured 216.3±326.4 kT/d², agreeing with 0 to within 0.66σ). The fix: add a sigma (the measured SEM) argument to observable(), z-test with err_sigma=(measured-predicted)/sigma, and wire both judge() and postmortem.py to prefer err_sigma over err_pct.
